clue.text: Substitute stable-boy — there's nowhere for him to sit here

definitions.text: there's nowhere for him to sit here

parts.note: a substitute is a stand-in, someone who takes another's place
a stable-boy who tends horses is a groom

explanation.surface: A replacement lad at the stables finds there is no seat for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing phrase: a place where a spectator has no seat but must stay on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Space in a theatre or ground without seats, where spectators stand throughout.

clue.text: Got rescued when in distress

indicators.note: something in distress is in a bad way, so the letters of the word before are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone was saved after getting into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got something is to have obtained or made sure of it, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Dress with a flared skirt, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver to say the skirt's name out loud and write down a word that sounds the same

parts.note: an A-line skirt is narrow at the waist and flares out towards the hem

explanation.surface: A frock with a skirt that flares out at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a garment, but it is the military verb: to dress ranks is to line soldiers up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing troops means bringing them into a straight line, the same as lining them up.

clue.text: Girls irritability gives rise to complaint

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and more than one of them gives Dis
irritability is bad temper

explanation.surface: Some young women's bad moods cause an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an ailment here, not a grumble; distemper is a disease of dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an illness, and distemper is a viral disease of animals such as dogs.

clue.text: When hands get together, nobody lacks energy

indicators.note: the word for nobody lacks, that is goes without, the letter for energy

parts.note: nobody means no one
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: When people join hands, no one has any vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hands' are a clock's: at twelve o'clock midday both point straight up together.
explanation.definitionFit: At midday the hour and minute hands of a clock overlap at twelve.

clue.text: When cut down, are glad rags found in a factory?

indicators.note: the word are is cut down by losing its opening letter

parts.note: glad rags are one's best clothes, one's finery

explanation.surface: Asks whether party clothes are made in a plant once they have been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims ARE to RE by losing its opening A; 'When' and 'found in a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial plant that purifies raw materials such as oil or sugar.

clue.text: Monks in command

explanation.surface: Friars under instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious order is a community of monks, and an order is also a command or instruction.

clue.text: Aspirate required to spell 'hanger-on'

indicators.note: the letters of the word before are rearranged so that they spell out a different word

explanation.surface: A grammar note: an aitch must be added to write a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspirate' suggests an H sound to add to a word, but it is simply the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off others, clinging to them as a sponger or hanger-on does.

clue.text: Cheat has to run away from church

parts.note: to run away is to flee
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A swindler must escape from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them out of money, a synonym for cheat.

clue.text: Crow flies other than straight, causing unnecessary alarm

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before are not left in a straight line but jumbled up

explanation.surface: A bird flying a crooked path startles everyone needlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as the crow flies' means in a straight line, so 'other than straight' sounds like a flight path.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the fable of the shepherd boy who kept raising false alarms about a predator.

clue.text: Entice pupil to speak slowly

parts.note: to entice is to draw someone in
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Tempt a schoolchild into talking at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened manner of talking, and to drawl is the verb for it.

clue.text: The best of the shearers spit

explanation.surface: The top sheep-shearer spits.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia the ringer is the fastest shearer in a shed; 'spit' is the noun, as in 'the spitting image'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringer is the top shearer in Australian slang, and a dead ringer is someone's exact double or spit.

clue.text: Batsman should be showing growth

parts.note: a cricket batsman should be in his crease, the marked line he must stay behind to be safe

explanation.surface: A cricketer ought to be developing.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is the painted line in cricket; a batsman out of it can be run out, so he should be in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a rise or growth in size or number.

clue.text: Pass university course in French town

parts.note: to pass away is to die
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a degree course at Oxford

explanation.surface: Succeed at a degree course in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' suggests passing an exam, but it is 'pass away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a Channel port on the coast of Normandy.

clue.text: Curse water on top of old vehicle

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, so a stretch of water
crate is slang for a rickety old car or plane

explanation.surface: Swear because the radiator water spilled over an ancient car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top of' puts the river first in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil upon, a formal synonym for curse.

clue.text: Pier isn't changed — it's in the original condition

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: The seaside pier has not been altered and is as it was built.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the pier is unchanged, yet 'changed' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine describes something unspoilt and as good as new.

clue.text: The main sort of block to be seen from the air when coming in to land

definitions.text: the air when coming in to land

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the sea
a breeze block is a light building block made with cinders

explanation.surface: A kind of building block glimpsed from an aircraft on its approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in to land' suggests an aircraft; it is moving air blowing from the sea onto the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea breeze is a wind blowing from the sea towards the coast during the day.

clue.text: Someone outstanding in competition

explanation.surface: A star performer in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is a stunning person, and also a contest where losers are eliminated round by round.

clue.text: Concerned about the French glade

indicators.note: the word for concerned goes about, that is around, the French article

parts.note: to be caring is to be concerned for others
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Worried about a woodland space in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearing is an open space in a forest, the same as a glade.

clue.text: Policeman with two characters in custody

explanation.surface: An officer with a pair of suspects locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: the first two letters of 'custody' are CU, the chemical symbol for this metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is slang for a police officer, and Cu is the symbol of the metal element.

clue.text: Father needs shelter, that's obvious

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: Dad must have some cover, that much is plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent, as in 'patently false', means plain and evident.

clue.text: Support expressed ambiguously in letters

indicators.note: the word after is set out in an unclear, muddled way, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Backing given in vague terms in correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like correspondence, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs holding up a table top or platform.

clue.text: Standard spear, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
a lance is a long spear carried by a horseman

explanation.surface: A regulation weapon, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of using words, an idiom or jargon.

clue.text: Correspond, getting a note in time

indicators.note: the musical note goes in, placed inside, the word for a period of time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Writing letters while a musician keeps tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree match up with each other, as figures correspond.

clue.text: Cursorily examine pitheads be fore closure of mine

indicators.note: the newspaper splits 'before' in two; it places the word for pitheads ahead of the next piece

parts.note: the brow is the top of a mine shaft, a pithead

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A quick look at colliery tops before the mine shuts down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be fore' is 'before' split across a line in the printed paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look through something casually without close study.

clue.text: The public promise to accept money

indicators.note: the word for promise takes in, so contains, the letter for money

parts.note: giving your word is making a promise
L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The people pledge to take cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The world can mean people in general, as in 'what will the world say?'

clue.text: Nasty eyesore, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is only part of the words before, a run of letters lying inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something ugly, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'extent' as the definition, which does not mean the answer; the whole clue defines it, a nasty sore on the eyelid, and also hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a painful red swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Record books always around

indicators.note: the word for always goes around, enclosing, the abbreviation for books

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Accounts that always surround the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter something is to write it in a register or log.

clue.text: Busy spinster May, say, turned over the cake

indicators.note: a spinster is unmarried, so the M for married is taken away

parts.note: May is an example of a month

indicators.note: the word for cake is turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: a torte is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman called May, kept busy, knocked over the gateau.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the usual abbreviation for married, so 'spinster' removes it from MONTH; 'turned over' reverses TORTE to ETROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the trot means continually on the go, kept busy without a break.

clue.text: People being given drugs may become nervous

explanation.surface: Patients receiving medicine may grow edgy.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal, an injection; the second is the British idiom for growing irritated or tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the needle is to receive an injection, and also slang for becoming annoyed or on edge.
